description: Input to the running game: a whole click on a Control or a 3D node named by path or by the words on it, an item chosen out of a menu, typing into the focus, or a raw action, key, mouse button, mouse motion or drag, touch or finger drag. All of it works headless, where the viewport is the project's window size and the GUI only takes what is inside it. On gdharness's own desktop, where a windowed run goes, Windows refuses to say where the pointer is: every pointer answer there carries pointer_on_hidden_desktop, and the run's first pointer_note says why it matters: get_mouse_position() on the root window, and what derives from it, reads nonsense, while what reads the event itself (the control under it, hover, tooltips, input handlers) gets the injected position. A native window no real pointer has entered gets no hover from Godot, so the runtime supplies it there and the answers say hover_supplied. Operations: click: press and release on a Control, a frame apart, named by nodePath or by says (found under nodePath when both are given), or on a 3D node where it is drawn. A control hidden in a ScrollContainer is scrolled to first; a RichTextLabel link is pressed where its words are drawn. A disabled button, a control that does not process and one mouse_behavior_recursive turned off are refused, since the press would do nothing; by says, a reachable one is picked over it; choose (needs nodePath): take an item out of a menu, by its words or its place in the list: the menu is opened, the item found as it stands then and pressed through the engine's own path, which needs no window and not ui_accept's binding. A disabled or hidden button in front of the menu is refused, and so is a press the menu did not take; action (needs action): press an action, or hold it; key (needs keycode): press a key, or hold it. Not for a menu a click has opened: an OptionButton or PopupMenu pops up as a window of its own that a key never reaches, so arrows move nothing and Enter closes it unchosen; choose selects there. Other windows are not like it: an embedded dialog whose owner reads keys in _input gets them; text (needs text): type a string into the field being edited, a character at a time, saying what it landed in and what it then holds (a secret field as its mask). With a dialog focused, the field is that dialog's focus, where the keys go; mouse_click (needs x, y): click a mouse button at a position, pressed and released a frame apart, each event carrying the buttons held after it; the answer says whole. A drag is mouse_drag. A wheel button is always a whole step, as a mouse sends one: a lone wheel press holds the viewport on the control that took it, so every later click lands there; mouse_motion (needs x, y): move the mouse to a position, carrying the distance from where the last injected event put it unless relativeX and relativeY say otherwise, and the buttons held; mouse_drag (needs x, y, toX, toY, frames): a whole drag in one call: press at x, y, a motion each frame, release at toX, toY; for a stir, a paint stroke or a slow slider; touch (needs x, y): press a finger at x, y and lift it a frame later, or hold it, as an InputEventScreenTouch; in the game's window the engine makes mouse events carrying DEVICE_ID_EMULATION from the first finger down, where emulate_mouse_from_touch is on (emulates_mouse); touch_drag (needs x, y, toX, toY, frames): mouse_drag for one finger: the touch, an InputEventScreenDrag each frame, and the lift; joypad_button (needs button): press a controller button, or hold it, as an InputEventJoypadButton, as a controller sends it to _input and _unhandled_input; an action bound to the button fires with it. Pressed and released a frame apart unless pressed says otherwise; joypad_motion (needs axis, value): move a stick or trigger axis to a value, as an InputEventJoypadMotion; the axis stays there until another motion moves it. The tool reference in the gdharness skill, and the site, say what every field of the answer means.

action.description: action: the InputMap action name. A Viewport never hands an action to a shortcut, so the buttons whose Shortcut holds the action are sent it as their Shortcut too, and pressed as by the key bound to it: one button at most, the last in the tree that takes it, passing over one that is disabled, hidden or outside its shortcut context. The answer names those buttons under shortcuts and the one pressed under shortcut_pressed, null when none took it. An engine dialog is not answered this way: AcceptDialog reads the Escape key itself and never asks the InputMap, so ui_cancel goes in and the question stays up. Dismiss one with the key op and keycode Escape, or click its button. Only for op action.

alt.description: key: hold Alt with it. Default false. Only for op key.

axis.description: joypad_motion: the stick or trigger axis, by name (left_x, left_y, right_x, right_y, trigger_left, trigger_right) or by its JoyAxis number. Only for op joypad_motion.

button.description: click, mouse_click, mouse_drag: left, right, middle, wheel_up or wheel_down, or a button number. Default left. joypad_button: the controller button, by name (a, b, x, y, back, guide, start, left_stick, right_stick, left_shoulder, right_shoulder, dpad_up, dpad_down, dpad_left, dpad_right, misc1, paddle1 to paddle4, touchpad) or by its JoyButton number; a, b, x and y are the bottom, right, left and top face buttons, as Godot names them, whatever the controller prints on them. Only for ops click, mouse_click, mouse_drag, joypad_button.

ctrl.description: key: hold Ctrl with it. Default false. Only for op key.

device.description: joypad_button, joypad_motion: which controller, counting from 0. Default 0. Only for ops joypad_button, joypad_motion.

doubleClick.description: click, mouse_click: default false. A double click is sent as one arrives from the system: a whole click, then a second press marked double_click and its release, so a button presses twice, as a player double-clicking it would. Only for ops click, mouse_click.

frames.description: mouse_drag, touch_drag: how many process frames the stroke takes, one motion each, as a real mouse or finger sends one a frame; a hand takes about 20 to 60 for a stroke across a screen. Only for ops mouse_drag, touch_drag.

holdFrames.description: action, key, mouse_click, joypad_button, touch: hold a whole press down for this many process frames and then let go, both inside the game, so a pour, a charge or a long press runs to a set length. A press, a frames wait and a release sent as three calls hold it for the time between the calls as well. The answer says held_frames, and under held_for the seconds the hold lasted and the physics_frames that ran in it: a process frame is no set time, and a headless game, drawing nothing, runs them far faster than the sixty physics ticks a second that _physics_process sees. Not with pressed, and not on a wheel step. Default 1. Only for ops action, key, mouse_click, joypad_button, touch.

index.description: click: which of several controls saying the words, counting from 0 in the order a refusal lists them, best matches first. choose: the item to take, by where it is in the list, when text will not do. touch, touch_drag: the finger, from 0, as InputEventScreenTouch.index; a second finger down at once is another index. Default 0. Only for ops click, choose, touch, touch_drag.

keycode.description: key: the key name, such as "Space" or "A", or its Godot keycode. Only for op key.

nodePath.description: click: the Control to click, at its centre, at x and y in its own space when those are given, or at the middle of the part on screen when no scroll brings its centre into view (said under pressed_on), or the 3D node to click, where it is drawn; with says, where to look for the control instead, default the whole tree. choose: the PopupMenu, or the OptionButton or MenuButton in front of one. mouse_click, mouse_motion, mouse_drag, touch, touch_drag: the Control, Node2D or Window whose own space the points are in, a Window's being its own pixels; the events go to the window that shows it, a native one included, which the game's window pixels cannot reach, and the answer names it under window when it is not the game's own. Default the game's window. Only for ops click, choose, mouse_click, mouse_motion, mouse_drag, touch, touch_drag.

pid.description: Which game, when several are running from one project, such as a bench and its workers: its process id, as editor_status lists under runtimes. Without it the game this server started or plays is the one asked when it is among them, and the answer says so under answeredBy; with one game per project it is not needed at all.

pressed.description: action, key, mouse_click, joypad_button, touch: leave it out and the press is a whole one, down and up a frame apart. true holds it down, false lets go of one being held, a finger lifted at x and y. A wheel button held down is still a whole step, since a wheel is never held. Only for ops action, key, mouse_click, joypad_button, touch.

projectPath.description: Which game, when more than one is running: the project directory it was started from. The pick without it, in order: the game this server started or is playing when it is among those running, named under answeredBy where there was a choice; else the only game there is; else a refusal naming every game and which argument tells them apart, pid when they are all one project and projectPath when they are not. Not needed with one game, nor for a call to this server's own.

relativeX.description: mouse_motion: the movement the event carries. Left out, it is the distance from where the last injected pointer event put the pointer, and none for the first; that is what a control that drags reads. Give it to send a motion the position does not show. Only for op mouse_motion.

relativeY.description: mouse_motion: as relativeX. Only for op mouse_motion.

replace.description: text: true writes over what the field already says, which is what filling one in means. Default false types at the caret, so a field reading 2.1 typed "0.3" at reads 2.10.3. The answer says what the field holds afterwards either way. A read-only field is refused. Only for op text.

says.description: click: the words on the control to click, matched the way runtime_inspect find matches says (a plain word is contained in the text, a pattern with * or ? is a glob over it, and | separates alternatives), among the controls on screen, and pressed in the same frame it was found in, so a panel rebuilding between a find and a click cannot free it first. Words on a label inside a button press the button. A control with something drawn over its centre that would take the pointer, such as a screen shown over it or a dialog stacked above its own, is not on screen; nor is one on a hidden canvas layer, one outside the viewport, or one a container clips away that a click does not scroll. The refusal counts those apart. The matches are ranked the way a person picks what to press: an enabled button before anything else, a disabled one included, then a control whose whole text, or one whole line of it such as the title on a card, is the words before one saying them as part of more, and the best one is pressed; found.picked says why. Several matches at the best rank are refused with each one listed, and index picks one. A match saying the words only as part of more is named under found.partOf, and is refused when another control says exactly the words (hidden, off the screen, covered, or on screen taking clicks without being a button), since it would stand in for that one, and when it lets the pointer through to what is under it; index presses it anyway. Words found only inside longer words ("out" in "Scout") rank after every other match and are refused unless index is given; words starting a longer word ("Recruit" in "Recruits") count. An empty field says its placeholder, and a control with no text of its own, a picture on a button, says its accessibility name. A tab, a list entry, a tree row and a menu bar title each count as a match of their own and are pressed where they are drawn, after their control scrolls them into view; a disabled one is refused. An item of an open menu is drawn by the menu rather than held as a control, so a click finds none, and the refusal names the menu and the choose call that picks it. Only for op click.

shift.description: key: hold Shift with it. Default false. Only for op key.

strength.description: action: 0 to 1. Default 1. Only for op action.

text.description: text: what to type. A newline is Enter and a tab is Tab, a space is a space, and "" with replace empties the field. choose: the item to take, by what it says as drawn, which in a game with translations is the translation; the key it holds is matched after that. An item whose whole words are these comes first; otherwise the words match as says does anywhere, a plain word as part of the item, a glob, or alternatives split at |, enabled items ahead of disabled ones, and several matching equally are refused with each listed. Only for ops text, choose.

toX.description: mouse_drag, touch_drag: where the release is, in window pixels or nodePath's own space. Only for ops mouse_drag, touch_drag.

toY.description: mouse_drag, touch_drag: as toX. Only for ops mouse_drag, touch_drag.

value.description: joypad_motion: where the axis is, -1 to 1: down and right are positive on a stick, and a trigger runs 0 to 1. The axis stays there until another motion moves it, as a stick held over does; send 0 to let it go back. Only for op joypad_motion.

via.description: mouse_drag, touch_drag: points the stroke passes through on the way, in order, each [x, y] in the space x and y are in. The motions are spread along the whole stroke by distance. Default none: a straight line. Only for ops mouse_drag, touch_drag.

x.description: click: with y, the point to press in the control's own space instead of its centre, for a control that draws its parts itself; not with a 3D node, nor with says finding an item the control draws. mouse_click, mouse_motion, touch: window pixels, or nodePath's own space when that is given. mouse_drag, touch_drag: where the press is, in the same space. Only for ops click, mouse_click, mouse_motion, mouse_drag, touch, touch_drag.

y.description: click, mouse_click, mouse_motion, mouse_drag, touch, touch_drag: as x. Only for ops click, mouse_click, mouse_motion, mouse_drag, touch, touch_drag.

name: runtime_input
title: Send input to the game
